record.paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
record.original_question: Classify g.o. spaces whose isotropy representation decomposes into two or three irreducible isotropy summands. Here M=G/K is a homogeneous space, m=T_o(G/K) is the tangent module at the origin, and the isotropy representation of K on m splits as a direct sum of two or three irreducible submodules; the task is to determine exactly which invariant metrics on such spaces make every geodesic an orbit of a one-parameter subgroup.

evidence.quote: two or three irreducible isotropy summands

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M = G/K be a connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with G a connected Lie group acting almost effectively by isometries and K a compact isotropy subgroup. Let g and k denote the Lie algebras of G and K, and fix a reductive decomposition g = k ⊕ m, where m is identified with the tangent space T_o(G/K) at the base point o = eK. The isotropy representation is the action of K (equivalently of Ad(K)) on m. A G-invariant Riemannian metric on G/K is called a geodesic orbit metric (g.o. metric) if every geodesic of (M, g) is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of G; the pair (G/K, g) is then called a g.o. space.

Problem. Assume that the isotropy representation of K on m decomposes as a direct sum of either exactly two or exactly three Ad(K)-irreducible submodules:
  m = m_1 ⊕ m_2   or   m = m_1 ⊕ m_2 ⊕ m_3.
Classify, up to equivalence, all pairs (G/K, g) of this form for which g is a g.o. metric. Equivalently, for each such homogeneous space G/K, determine explicitly all G-invariant Riemannian metrics that are geodesic orbit metrics.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-isotropy-summand case for compact simply connected g.o. spaces has been classified by Chen and Nikonorov (Geometriae Dedicata, 2019, and follow-up work). The three-summand case has been treated in several specific settings (e.g., simple isotropy group, rank-two compact Lie groups, Stiefel bundles, strongly isotropy irreducible building blocks), but a complete general classification does not appear to be available; the broader classification of g.o. manifolds remains an active open problem.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic orbit Riemannian spaces with two isotropy summands. I
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of compact simply connected geodesic orbit Riemannian spaces (G/H, g) with two irreducible submodules in the isotropy representation.

status_evidence.title: Compact geodesic orbit spaces with a simple isotropy group
status_evidence.snippet: Studies g.o. condition for compact spaces with simple isotropy, including cases with few summands.
status_evidence.claim: Three-summand case treated in specific subcases, not complete in general.

status_evidence.title: A review of compact geodesic orbit manifolds and the g.o. condition for SU(5)/S(U(2)×U(2))
status_evidence.snippet: Review noting that the full classification of g.o. manifolds remains open and reporting progress in low-summand cases.
status_evidence.claim: General classification still open; partial progress in few-summand cases.
